question: Which of the following is the easternmost range of the Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Purvanchal Range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Purvanchal Range is the easternmost extension of the Himalayas in India.
 
• It includes hills like the Patkai, Naga, Mizo, and Manipur hills located in the northeastern region of India.
 
• The range runs along the eastern boundary of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura.
 
• The Purvanchal Range is known for its dense forests, rich biodiversity, and unique ethnic communities.
 
• It is geologically younger compared to the western ranges of the Himalayas and is composed primarily of sedimentary rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayan Ranges:**

 
 
• The Himalayas are divided into three main ranges: the Greater Himalayas (Himadri), the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and the Outer Himalayas (Shivaliks).
 
• The Purvanchal Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas and forms the easternmost extension of the mountain system.
 
 
 
• **Patkai Hills:**
 
 
• Located in Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland, the Patkai Hills are part of the Purvanchal Range and serve as a natural boundary between India and Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **Naga Hills:**
 
 
• These hills are situated in Nagaland and are known for their unique tribal culture and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Purvanchal Range is home to diverse flora and fauna, including many endemic species due to its tropical and subtropical climate.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The range plays a significant role in India's northeastern connectivity and serves as a strategic frontier with neighboring countries like Myanmar and China.
